elements.evidence: Revised 22.14 reads "M&I shall not solicit the employees of Customer during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason." The former mutual formulation ("Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party") is gone, so the only restricted party is the Vendor; no operative language elsewhere in the cited text binds Customer not to solicit, employ, engage or induce M&I personnel.

The rendered clause runs one way only ("M&I shall not solicit the employees of Customer"); there is no reciprocal obligation on Customer. This is intentional at the preferred level but defeats the fallback element.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: The clause still covers "the employees of Customer" without limitation to personnel directly involved in the Services.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Duration remains "during the Term of this Agreement", and "Term" is defined as ending on the eighth anniversary of the Commencement Date (p0049); no 12-month post-involvement tail is stated.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: No carve-out sentence for general advertisements or general solicitations was inserted; the clause bars solicitation "for any reason".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: No carve-out for responses to unsolicited approaches appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits only soliciting employees; it contains no "employ or engage", "hire" or "no-hire" language, so hiring as such is not barred.
Cross-check: even measured against the fallback checklist, the Customer-side burden is fully removed, but the fallback level as a whole remains incomplete for the reasons above.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element (no non-solicitation restriction on Customer) is met by converting Section 22.14 from a mutual bar into a one-way bar on M&I only.

Fallback level is incomplete (not mutual, not scoped to personnel directly involved, no 12-month post-involvement limit, no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is fully satisfied and the offer of a compliant mutual alternative is correctly confined to the margin comment rather than the operative text.

Minimality holds: the only operative change is the party direction of Section 22.14 ("Neither party ... the other party" to "M&I ... Customer"). Retained favourable language ("during the Term", "for any reason") is untouched, no carve-outs, survival tails or procedures were added, and the reproduced Term definition at p0049 is unedited.

Intent preserved: the Vendor-side restriction, its temporal anchor to the defined "Term", and all cross-references survive intact; no undefined term, dangling reference or contradictory retained sentence is created, and the Term definition continues to operate for the retained obligation.

Finding classification as a deviation is sound: the original clause covered all Vendor and Customer employees for roughly eight years with no carve-outs, which fails the fallback on scope, duration and carve-outs and sits in walk-away territory (over 24 months, all personnel), while stopping short of a no-hire.
